course_description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of foodservice systems in a variety of settings, such as hospitals, aged care homes, early childhood education centres, schools, sporting organisations and commercial food businesses. Students will explore the role of the foodservice dietitian and examine how food systems underpin nutrition care across diverse settings. This course critically examines foodservice operations and processes involved in delivering food and mealtime experiences that are safe, nutritious, and responsive to consumer preferences, while ensuring regulatory compliance and alignment with organisational objectives. Content will focus on food procurement, production and distribution, menu planning and assessment, recipe development and modification, food safety, risk management, quality improvement, and management of human and financial resources. This course will prepare students for their foodservice management placement.

course_aims: This course aims to develop advanced skills and knowledge in food service management that is relevant to dietetics professionals.

learning_outcomes.description: Analyse foodservice management principles and systems and discuss the role of dietitians across diverse foodservice settings.

Develop, adapt and assess recipes and menus for diverse populations and settings, ensuring alignment with evidence-based nutrition standards or guidelines and incorporating nutritional, cultural, operational, consumer and sustainability considerations.
Critically evaluate and apply food safety and risk management frameworks to support regulatory, and organisational compliance.
Apply organisational management, financial management, human resources, change management and quality improvement principles and activities to support effective foodservice systems and operations.
Identify and explain opportunities for continuous quality improvement to enhance service delivery, consumer satisfaction, and organisational outcomes.

Workshop 2- Governance Landscape, Food Safety and Risk Management Students are required to complete the 'Governance Landscape, Food Safety and Risk Management' Module before attending the workshop.
Workshop 3- The Menu Students are required to complete the Module 'The Menu' before attending the workshop.
Workshop 4- Quality and Satisfaction Students are required to complete the 'Quality and Satisfaction' Module before attending the workshop.

Workshop 5- Foodservice Inputs, Food Product Flow and Kitchen Design Students are required to complete the 'Foodservice Inputs, Food Product Flow and Kitchen Design' Module before attending the workshop.
Workshop 5- Application to Practice During this workshop, students will visit a foodservice operation. See Blackboard for site details and location.
Workshop 6- Procurement, Production, Distribution and Service Students are required to complete the 'Procurement, Production, Distribution and Service' Module before attending the workshop.

Workshop 7- Service, Mealtime Experience, Dining Environment and Sanitation Students are required to complete the 'Service, Mealtime Experience, Dining Environment and Sanitation' Module before attending the workshop.
Workshop 7- Application to Practice During this workshop, students will visit a foodservice operation. See Blackboard for site details and location.
Workshop 8- Human, Financial and Operational Management Students are required to complete the 'Human, Financial and Operational Management' Module before attending the workshop.
